title: Comprehensive Eyelid & Limbal Oncology Portfolio
summary: An exhaustive clinical guide covering pediatric limbal dermoids, malignant eyelid tumors like Squamous Cell Carcinoma, and the specific management protocols for aggressive sebaceous gland carcinomas. This poster bridges clinical presentation with surgical and histopathological pearls for the ophthalmic specialist.

sections.title: Pediatric Case: Limbal Dermoid
content: Case: An 8-year-old patient presented with the this finding.
Q1: Describe what you are seeing.
Q2: How would you manage this patient?
Clinical Pearl: Limbal dermoids are choristomas. If associated with preauricular skin tags or vertebral anomalies, consider Goldenhar Syndrome.
Management options: Observation (if asymptomatic), or surgical excision with lamellar keratoplasty if causing significant astigmatism or visual axis obstruction.

sections.title: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC) Clinical Presentation
sections.content: A1: This an image of an old man/ lady showing left temporal upper lid swelling with hyperemia and ulceration with temporal mild lower lid hyperemia and swelling associated with temporal upper lid ptosis. In addition, there is temporal eyebrow hair loss with temporal periocular skin hyperpigmentation.

rows: Acute inflammation of tissues anterior to the orbital septum.
Painful, focal inflammatory lesion of meibomian glands.
May arise from actinic keratosis; carries risk of perineural invasion.
Most common; pearly borders; telangiectasia; rarely metastasizes.
The 'Great Masquerader'; high mortality; skip lesions.
Violaceous nodule; highly aggressive; associated with polyomavirus.

sections.title: Malignant Eyelid Workup Protocol
content: Step 1: Q1: Describe the photo? Q2: What is your ddx? Q3: If I told you that this photo represents a biopsy taken that confirm squamous cell carcinoma. What will you do next?
Step 2: Diagnosis: Perform incisional biopsy with adequate margin for histopathology.
Step 3: Surgical Planning: First-line treatment is surgical excision. Radiation therapy is the second-best treatment.
Step 4: Non-Surgical Options: Topical imiquimod and topical or injectable interferon (for elderly non-surgical candidates).
Step 5: Education: Inform patients about the etiologic role of the sun.
Step 6: Systemic Referral: Refer to oncologist or internist for regional/systemic workup and surveillance.
Step 7: Imaging: SCC requires CT of the brain and orbit to check infiltration (lacrimal gland) or perineural invasion (PNI).
Step 8: Nodes: Check sentinel lymph nodes (LNs) and local LNs for lymphadenopathy with metastasis.
Step 9: Distance Check: PET scan for distant metastasis.

rows: Wide margins necessary due to 'Skip Lesions'.

sections.title: Special Focus: Sebaceous Gland Carcinoma (SGC)
content: NB for Sebaceous cell CA: Wide excision (5mm) is MANDATORY due to skip lesions.
Send fresh tissue specifically for Oil Red O stain (to identify lipid).
Perform Conjunctival Map Biopsies: From at least 4 bulbar quadrants + medial and lateral tarsal conjunctiva (upper & lower lids).
If map biopsy is positive: Adjunctive cryotherapy is required.
Regional Management: Sentinel LN biopsy; KIV neck dissection for regional adenopathy.
Reconstruction: Repair lid defect depending on size and margin involvement.

branches: CT Orbits/MRI with Contrast: SCC, SGC, Malignant Melanoma
MRI Brain/Orbit: Check for Orbital/Intracranial extension
BCC Medial Canthal: Check Lacrimal sac or Orbital involvement
PET Scan: Evaluation for distant metastasis

sections.title: Management of Incomplete Margins
content: Q4: After excision, the edge of the excised sample is infiltrated with tumor cells. What to do next?
A4: If the excisional biopsy showed incomplete excision with unsafety margin, re-excise more of the margin to confirm clearance.
Following confirmed clearance via frozen section or Mohs, proceed with eyelid reconstruction.

content.explanation: For BCC with orbital/intracranial extension not amenable to surgery/radiation, use targeted therapy with Hedgehog pathway inhibitors (e.g., Vismodegib).
